question.problem:
Consider the function $f:R\to {R}^{3},$ defined by 

$$
f(x)=[\begin{aligned}x \\ {x}^{2} \\ {x}^{3}\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the total derivative of $f$ with respect to $x?$

Consider the vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}: \mathbb{R}^{4} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^2$ defined by

What is $\dfrac{\textrm{d} \mathbf{f}}{\textrm{d} \mathbf{x}},$ the total derivative of $\mathbf{f}$ with respect to $\mathbf{x}$ at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14217875/assets/9e3db521c6069277f54b17ce029b67b21af322398d1d295101cf5b91ee0c6952.svg)
current_example.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}: \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^m$ with respect to a vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ is the $m \times n$ matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14217875/assets/a09a9f3d73d609900c44e2881bfb59d36f2860ab3783756136ffe9f5fd604798.svg)

In our case, writing out the function $\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x})$ where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14217875/assets/2a41adce803b7b81e6d57cb6340c503a1fe09fe850d095d3c1fa4e8697985495.svg), we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14217875/assets/c9bb140c1c026e5a7fbf115cbc5d91e2111b2c1ed9cedc2f105977fa8c3cdcf4.svg)

From here, we have $f_1(\mathbf{x}) = x_1 + 2x_2 + 4x_3 + 8x_4$ and $f_2(\mathbf{x}) = x_1 + 3x_2 + 9x_3 +27x_4.$ So, the total derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{3}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{4}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{3}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{4}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 & 8 \\ 1 & 3 & 9 & 27\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Since the total derivative is a constant matrix, evaluating it at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14217875/assets/373c4c097700e9a59afa0e20e4e9e453b918209084e019970cb97402b7e57069.svg) gives the same matrix.
